QuestionStmt.S: If a galvanometer is shunted by $\left(\frac{1}{n-1}\right)^{\text{th}}$ of the value of its resistance, then the fraction of the total current passing through the galvanometer is

Solution.S:
Let galvanometer resistance be G. Shunt resistance S = $\frac{G}{n-1}$.

Current through galvanometer: $I_g = \frac{S}{G + S} I$.

Substitute S:

$$I_g = \frac{G/(n-1)}{G + G/(n-1)} I = \frac{1/(n-1)}{1 + 1/(n-1)} I = \frac{1/(n-1)}{(n)/(n-1)} I = \frac{1}{n} I$$

Thus, fraction of total current through galvanometer = $\frac{1}{n}$.

Final Answer: $$\boxed{\frac{1}{n}}$$

Hence, the correct option is B.
